title: Your training split and friends
summary: Build a training split around your own workouts. Start with Upper / Lower, Push / Pull / Legs, full body every other day or Cardio, then edit the repeating cycle and rest days. Home follows your saved schedule. Friends and Home show when your friends are working out, active now or were last active, with the workout they are doing. Choose what friends see with separate Online status and Live workouts switches. Browse exercises by their muscle credits, choose when partial sets count, and review your weekly training. Discover public profiles in Find, see RPE and set types in colour, get rest alerts while browsing Relay, and open release notes from Notifications. Profiles show the five latest cardio sessions at a time, with page controls for browsing older sessions.
changes: Open Your split in Settings > Training, or choose Edit split on Home. Pick an Upper / Lower, Push / Pull / Legs, FBEOD or Cardio template, or start custom.

Name your split, choose its start date, add and reorder workout or rest days, and preview upcoming weeks. Each step is one calendar day; cycles continue across weeks, so full body every other day stays every other day.

Use built-in workout types or create your own, including Full body A and Full body B. Home and the Start menu keep each custom type separate when suggesting exercises from its previous session. Starting without a previous session still selects the scheduled workout type.

Your split is saved to your account. Home shows scheduled rest days, refreshes the schedule after local midnight, and asks you to update your split if a scheduled workout type is removed. Logging or skipping a workout does not change the calendar cycle.
Switch off Use this split and save to return to automatic workout suggestions while keeping your saved pattern. Accounts without a saved split keep the existing automatic recommendations.

Friends shows when each friend is working out, active now or was last active. A friend's workout in progress moves to the top with a Live label, its name and how long they have been training, and stays while their phone is locked between sets. Changes appear as they happen.
Home's Recent Friends Activity lists friends working out first, showing their live workout in place of their last session until they finish.

Settings > Account & privacy > Profile sharing has a Live activity section with separate Online status and Live workouts switches and a preview of what friends see. Both start on, only accepted friends can see them, and turning one off hides it from friends straight away.

Exercises has a question-mark button beside every lift for its direct and partial muscle credits. Muscle filters include all exercises currently contributing to that muscle, including 0.5-set assistance, instead of matching only the exercise label.

The exercise list shows 10 lifts per page by default. Use the three-line options button to choose 10, 20, 50 or 100, and the previous, next or page-picker controls to browse. Search, muscle and sort changes return to page one; returning from exercise details keeps the page.

Count partial sets is saved from the selected week for each exercise and carries forward until the next change. Earlier weeks keep their choices, and totals use the setting on each workout date. Direct credits always count; muscle mappings are unchanged.

Sets per muscle is on Home and at the bottom of Training. Weekly totals use each workout’s saved credit setting. Show more reveals remaining trained and untrained muscles, and each muscle opens its contributing exercises and workouts.
Home keeps the date above its header, with the title and action buttons aligned on one row at phone widths. Very narrow screens use a left-aligned action row.
Volume records now say Volume PR for this weight on set badges, popups and record lists, making the same-weight comparison clear.
Swipe through saved equipment photos while logging. Deleting an old photo removes its workout attachments after confirmation and keeps the recorded sets.
Saved workout sets use subtle type colours in Profile and Training history: orange warm-ups, green working sets, purple drop sets and red failed sets.
Removed the Exercise note for next time field from workout exercise cards. Previously saved exercise notes remain in workout history.

Social > Find automatically suggests public accounts you are not already connected to, eight per page with numbered, Previous and Next controls. Each person's username appears beneath their name. Tap a name or avatar to open the profile, or use Add friend separately. Your account, existing friends and requests, private and disabled accounts, and blocks in either direction are excluded. Search remains available above the suggestions.

Notifications includes a Relay release row with its version, title, date and View button. View opens What's new and clears New; closing the notes returns to Notifications; opening the inbox alone does not. The latest release remains available after viewing, and its read state is kept per account and release on this device. The row counts towards the 15-notification page limit and stays available if social notifications cannot load.

Rest complete now appears as a nonblocking in-app alert while Relay is visible, including when you are on another tab or have dismissed the countdown. Background phone notifications keep their existing delivery path. Cancelled rests do not trigger an alert.

Recent Friends Activity on Home shows the original logged time in your local time beside Today, Yesterday or the session date, for strength and cardio sessions. Editing a workout does not change its logged time.
The top-right Settings icon always opens All settings, instead of returning to the last section. Settings search still opens the selected control and unfinished forms stay available.
Equipment photo opens directly to its photo controls, with the redundant introductory sentence removed.

RPE numbers use an effort scale: green at 5 and 6, lime at 7, gold at 8, orange at 9 and red at 10, with colours between those values for half points. The selected RPE and folded set summary use the same colour; blank values stay neutral. Light mode uses darker text colours.

Workout rows now follow their set type: orange warm-ups, green working sets, purple drop sets and red failure sets. The tint stays consistent while editing, after completion and on suggested sets. RPE changes do not change the row type or its colour.

Your profile and shared profiles show five cardio sessions per page, newest first. Use the previous and next arrows or the page picker to browse older sessions, including sessions beyond the former latest-20 limit.
The Cardio header shows the visible range and total. Your selected page stays in place during profile updates, and a failed page request can be retried without losing the current page.

highlights.title: Your training split
highlights.description: Build a training split around your own workouts. Start with Upper / Lower, Push / Pull / Legs, full body every other day or Cardio, then edit the repeating cycle and rest days. Home follows your saved schedule.

highlights.title: See who's training
highlights.description: Friends working out move to the top with a Live row, the workout name and how long they have been training. Everyone else shows Active now or when they were last active.

image.alt: Social Friends tab with two synthetic friends working out at the top, each with a Live row showing the workout name and time so far, then friends active now and active 2h ago.

highlights.title: Live workouts on Home
highlights.description: Recent Friends Activity lists friends working out first, with their live workout in place of their last session.

image.alt: Home's Recent Friends Activity with two synthetic friends' live workouts first, followed by other friends' latest sessions and reaction buttons.

highlights.title: You choose what friends see
highlights.description: Live activity in Profile sharing has separate Online status and Live workouts switches, with a preview of what friends see.

image.alt: Live activity settings with Online status and Live workouts switched on and a preview showing a synthetic account as Active now.

highlights.title: Exercises, ten at a time
highlights.description: Use the question mark beside a lift for muscle credits and the three-line button to change page size. Filters include direct and enabled partial credits.

image.alt: Training exercise list with a question-mark help button beside each lift, list options and Page 1 of 4.

highlights.title: Keep each week’s partial-set choices
highlights.description: Choose a week in an exercise’s question-mark popup. Count partial sets carries forward until changed again, while earlier weeks keep their setting.

image.alt: Leg Press week-of selector on 5 October with partial adductors off and direct glute and quad credits retained.

highlights.title: See every weekly muscle total
highlights.description: The weekly muscle card is on Home and at the bottom of Training. Show more reveals remaining trained and untrained muscles.

image.alt: Weekly muscle totals with 4 direct glute and quad sets and 2 partial adductor set credits.

highlights.title: Keep Home’s header aligned
highlights.description: The date sits above the title, with all five action buttons beside Home at phone widths. Very narrow screens use a left-aligned action row.

image.alt: Home header at 393px with the date above and all five action buttons aligned beside the title.

highlights.title: Manage equipment photos while logging
highlights.description: Swipe through saved machines. Confirming deletion removes an old photo and its workout attachments while keeping the sets.

image.alt: Swiping both ways through saved equipment photos, cancelling deletion, then deleting an older photo while preserving the workout sets and another pin.

highlights.title: Suggested friends in Find
highlights.description: Find automatically lists public accounts you are not connected to, eight per page, with usernames beneath their names. Tap a name or avatar to open the profile; Add friend is separate.

image.alt: Social Find automatically listing eight fictional public profiles with usernames beneath their names, separate Add friend buttons, a 1-8 of 17 range and numbered pagination in a phone-sized view.

highlights.title: RPE effort and set types in colour
highlights.description: RPE numbers run from green through orange to red, including half points. Row tints follow the set type and stay consistent while editing or completing a set.

image.alt: Workout table with orange warm-up, green working, purple drop and red failure rows, plus coloured RPE numbers; the green working set is being edited at RPE 10. Isolated sample data.

highlights.title: Release notes in Notifications
highlights.description: The latest Relay release has its own inbox row. Tap View for What's new; closing the notes returns to the inbox. New clears after viewing and the row stays available.

image.alt: Notifications with a Relay 1.0.1 release row, New indicator, title, date and View button, above synthetic friend activity.

highlights.title: Rest alerts while you browse
highlights.description: Rest complete appears above your current screen, even after dismissing the countdown. The alert leaves navigation available; background phone notifications keep their existing delivery path.

image.alt: Rest complete appears above Body while a synthetic workout remains active, after dismissing the countdown and leaving the workout screen.
